description:
## Empirical signal (2026-05-04)

Surfaced during ariadne--m20 autonomous-mode coordination. Both POLYBIUS seats running fixed */5 min polling cadence revealed two failure modes: (1) PRINCIPAL got impatient during active review windows (5-min round-trip felt slow during an iterative section), and (2) quiet periods burned cron fires for nothing (just heartbeats, no substantive content).

PRINCIPAL flagged: 'I think we need a flexible polling frequency depending upon the complexity of the task being handed off.'

## The pattern

Three cadence regimes per coordination:

1. **Active** (proposal posted, review pending) — */2 min polling, max responsiveness for fast iteration cycles. Burns more fires but only during short active windows.

2. **Default** (steady-state, between active proposals) — */5 min polling. The current standard.

3. **Quiet** (long-running watch, only radio checks active, no substantive proposals in flight) — */15 or */30 min polling. Detects peer death without burning fires for nothing.

## Mechanism

Each section/handoff comment includes a complexity tag:

- '[complexity: simple]' — one-line / mechanical / unambiguous → default cadence sufficient
- '[complexity: medium]' — substantive review needed but bounded → default cadence
- '[complexity: complex]' — substantial design judgment, iteration likely → both sides switch to active cadence for the duration

Both peers read the tag on their next fire and adjust their own cron via CronDelete + CronCreate. After section closes, both peers drop back to default. After 30+ min of no-activity, both peers drop to quiet.

## Cost framing

Cadence trade-off:
- */2 (active): 30 fires/hour — high but bounded to short windows (~30 min/section max)
- */5 (default): 12 fires/hour — current
- */15 (quiet): 4 fires/hour — 67% reduction during long stretches

Net for a typical engagement: substantially fewer total fires AND better responsiveness when it matters.

## Where in substrate

Should integrate with the radio-check pattern (stoa--ivc) since both are POLYBIUS-pair coordination protocol. Likely lives in operating-disciplines.md (universal team pattern) or as a §7.4 extension in MAJOR_POLYBIUS.

DAEDALUS to design the integration with stoa--ivc; ARGUS to critique the cadence-switching mechanism for race conditions (what if peer's cron updates out of sync with mine).

## Cloud cron implications

Cloud scheduled tasks have a 1-hour minimum cadence. Active/quiet regimes can't be implemented for cloud-watching directly. The pattern applies cleanly to local crons only. For cloud-watching, the right shape is a single fixed-hourly cron with a fast-trigger escalation: if cloud poll detects substantive new content, it surfaces to PRINCIPAL who can then spin up a local active-cadence cron for the duration.

## Reference

- ariadne--m20 (active engagement that surfaced this)
- stoa--ivc (radio-check pattern, sibling protocol concern)
- §7.4 of MAJOR_POLYBIUS (current polling capability discipline)
- operating-disciplines.md (substrate-deployed team patterns from stoa--vz9)
title: Adaptive polling cadence for POLYBIUS-pair coordination (active/default/quiet regimes)
